questions.prompt: What does a faux-provider test check?
options: Whether the real model chooses the right tool
Whether your tools, gates and rewrites behave correctly when the model says a known thing
Whether the model writes good English
questions.explanation: The replies are scripted, so the model decides nothing. The test checks the pack's own code against known replies.

questions.prompt: A test queues one reply, and the session then makes a second model call. What happens?
options: The first reply is played again
The faux provider returns an error saying no more responses are queued
The session asks a real provider
The test passes without a result
questions.explanation: When the queue is empty, the reply is the error "No more faux responses queued". It tells you that you scripted too few replies.

questions.prompt: Why do you still need golden tasks with a real model if faux tests pass?
options: Faux tests cannot run a gate
A scripted model never decides anything, so faux tests say nothing about the expert's judgement
Golden tasks do not need a fixture
questions.explanation: Faux replies are fixed in advance. Only a real model shows whether the expert picks the right tool and refuses the right requests.
